chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who forgets the ghusl on Friday until he has prayed. He said: If there is still time, then he must perform ghusl and repeat the salat; but if the time has passed, then his salat has been valid.

So the proper way regarding this report is that we understand it as referring to a kind of recommendation, not obligation and requirement. Likewise, what has been narrated concerning making up the ghusl of Friday on the following day, and performing it earlier on Thursday if missing it is feared, is to be understood as recommendation.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the ritual prayer that may be repeated if time remains
key_terms.الْغُسْلَ: the ritual bath, here referring to the Friday ghusl
key_terms.الْفَوْتُ: missing the act or its proper time
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, the day on which this recommended ghusl is performed

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets the Friday ghusl and prays, must he repeat the salat?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of one who forgot the Friday ghusl until after performing salat. The narration states that if time remains, he performs ghusl and repeats the salat, but if the time has passed, the salat stands; the compiler then clarifies that this is to be understood in the sense of recommendation rather than obligation.
